text.p: Musicland Stores Corp said it will not file its form 10-K annual report with the Securities and Exchange Commission on time, but expected to file the report by the middle of April.

The retailer needs additional time to complete appropriate disclosures to address discussions it is having with its banks to obtain amendments to its credit agreements, the company said in a recent SEC filing.
Musicland said last month its bank group extended waivers of existing financial covenants and technical defaults through May 29.

"If an amendment is not obtained by May 29, 1997, when the waivers under the credit agreement expire, the company will be in default and the banks could demand repayment of all amounts outstanding under the revolver," the company said in the SEC filing.
In February, Musicland reported a net loss of $193.7 million, or $5.80 a share for 1996, compared with a loss of $135.8 million, or $4 a share, in 1995.
The 1996 loss included goodwill writedown of $95.3 million and restructuring charges of $75 million, the company said.
Musicland shares were down 1/8 at 1-1/8 Wednesday.
